And clicking (52,44) (frame 26) — that's the slot in the lower box, a no-op.
Plan: use chamber movement: LEFT, LEFT, RIGHT, RIGHT (4 actions, chamber ends up in the same place), then... we need exactly 6 more to reach 14: LEFT×3? The chamber is at (15,55), and LEFT goes to (15,49),(15,43),(15,37)... and to return RIGHT×3: 6 actions total, chamber returns to (15,55).
After that, click piece 13 (16,14) → expect a ring at (25,15). Then click (16,26) to execute. Then repeat: piece 25 → ring 37 → click; piece 43 → ring 31 → click → upper box to 1... wait, sequence: pieces 13,19,31,43:
1. Click 13 → ring 25; click 25 → pieces 25,31,43.
2. Click 25 → ring 37; click 37 → pieces 37,43... no wait: 25 over 31 → 37: pieces 37,43? 31 disappears? No: the jump removes source 25 and 31, and places 37. Result: 37,43.
3. Click 43 → ring 31; click 31 → pieces 31. → 1 in the upper box! The lower box is already at 1 → character appears, pieces get consumed → both boxes empty, character appears.
Then the character phase: in wave 1, after that I moved the chamber and clicked the character → a new wave. But wait — the goal might be different: when the character appears, click the character? Or dock the chamber on the character? I don't know the win condition for level 2. In wave 1, when the character appeared, the box got new pieces (wave 2). Maybe level 2 = multiple waves; clear all waves? Or the character is the final "delivery" target: the chamber delivers the collected pieces to the character?
Hmm, wait, actually let me reconsider: at the end of wave 1 (frame 39), all pieces including the lower (51,43) disappeared. Then a character appeared. So wave clear = both boxes to 1 or fewer? The lower box was 1 from the start... and got cleared along with the upper box. So the lower box's piece gets consumed when the upper box is cleared?? Or the lower box's piece was a "starter" that gets consumed at the start of the wave...
Honestly, the immediate next step is clear: fill the counter to 14 with 6 filler actions, then execute the jump. Even if the threshold is different, the clicks after that will tell us.
Filler: LEFT×3, RIGHT×3 (chamber stays docked). Wait — the chamber at (15,55): LEFT → (15,49): is this a valid position? In wave 1, (33,55) → RIGHT was no-op (at the end). At (15,55) is UP no-op? <tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>

def orpos():
    for n in current_frame.segmentation['nodes']:
        if n['color']=='O':
            r0=min(p[0] for p in n['boundary']); c0=min(p[1] for p in n['boundary'])
            return (r0,c0)
def state():
    N=[]; rings=[]
    for n in current_frame.segmentation['nodes']:
        r0=min(p[0] for p in n['boundary']); c0=min(p[1] for p in n['boundary'])
        if n['color']=='N' and n['pixels']==12:
            N.append((r0,c0))
        elif n['color']=='g' and n['pixels']<=4:
            rings.append((r0,c0))
    return sorted(N), sorted(rings)
action(['LEFT','LEFT','LEFT','RIGHT','RIGHT','RIGHT'])
print("O:", orpos(), "row0:", current_frame.ascii.split('\n')[0][:16])
action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':16,'col':14}])
print("after click13:", state())
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

g count = 8. If the threshold is 14, we need 6 more actions. But wait — the w counter in wave 1 started at 2 at step 13, and reached 14 at step 27 (12 actions). Level 2 started at step ~11-13 with w=2... actually maybe the counter was already at 1-2 when level 2 started (carried over from level 1? Level 1 had its own counter).
The threshold is probably 14 (when the bar filled up with w, the box became active). The g counter is now at 8 → 6 more.
Which actions should be fillers? Safe, reversible: move the chamber LEFT then RIGHT (2 actions each cycle), or click empty cells. But caution: each click on an empty cell in the upper box might place a ring?? In wave 1, clicking empty slot (16,56) (frame 29) erased the ring! And clicking (52,44) (frame 26) — that's the slot in the lower box, a no-op.
Plan: use chamber movement: LEFT, LEFT, RIGHT, RIGHT (4 actions, chamber ends up in the same place), then... we need exactly 6 more to reach 14: LEFT×3? The chamber is at (15,55), and LEFT goes to (15,49),(15,43),(15,37)... and to return RIGHT×3: 6 actions total, chamber returns to (15,55).
After that, click piece 13 (16,14) → expect a ring at (25,15). Then click (16,26) to execute. Then repeat: piece 25 → ring 37 → click; piece 43 → ring 31 → click → upper box to 1... wait, sequence: pieces 13,19,31,43:
1. Click 13 → ring 25; click 25 → pieces 25,31,43.
2. Click 25 → ring 37; click 37 → pieces 37,43... no wait: 25 over 31 → 37: pieces 37,43? 31 disappears? No: the jump removes source 25 and 31, and places 37. Result: 37,43.
3. Click 43 → ring 31; click 31 → pieces 31. → 1 in the upper box! The lower box is already at 1 → character appears, pieces get consumed → both boxes empty, character appears.
Then the character phase: in wave 1, after that I moved the chamber and clicked the character → a new wave. But wait — the goal might be different: when the character appears, click the character? Or dock the chamber on the character? I don't know the win condition for level 2. In wave 1, when the character appeared, the box got new pieces (wave 2). Maybe level 2 = multiple waves; clear all waves? Or the character is the final "delivery" target: the chamber delivers the collected pieces to the character?
Hmm, wait, actually let me reconsider: at the end of wave 1 (frame 39), all pieces including the lower (51,43) disappeared. Then a character appeared. So wave clear = both boxes to 1 or fewer? The lower box was 1 from the start... and got cleared along with the upper box. So the lower box's piece gets consumed when the upper box is cleared?? Or the lower box's piece was a "starter" that gets consumed at the start of the wave...
Honestly, the immediate next step is clear: fill the counter to 14 with 6 filler actions, then execute the jump. Even if the threshold is different, the clicks after that will tell us.
Filler: LEFT×3, RIGHT×3 (chamber stays docked). Wait — the chamber at (15,55): LEFT → (15,49): is this a valid position? In wave 1, (33,55) → RIGHT was no-op (at the end). At (15,55) is UP no-op? LEFT should be valid (the track extends to the left). Let's batch-execute: LEFT, LEFT, LEFT, RIGHT, RIGHT, RIGHT, then click (16,14), and check the ring.

def orpos():
    for n in current_frame.segmentation['nodes']:
        if n['color']=='O':
            r0=min(p[0] for p in n['boundary']); c0=min(p[1] for p in n['boundary'])
            return (r0,c0)
def state():
    N=[]; rings=[]
    for n in current_frame.segmentation['nodes']:
        r0=min(p[0] for p in n['boundary']); c0=min(p[1] for p in n['boundary'])
        if n['color']=='N' and n['pixels']==12:
            N.append((r0,c0))
        elif n['color']=='g' and n['pixels']<=4:
            rings.append((r0,c0))
    return sorted(N), sorted(rings)
